text: The label mismatch is fixed and guarded. What's left is the hard part: telling Fairmont's leadership and the affected elevator managers exactly what happened, in plain language.

The sentence that matters most: this was a telemetry gap, not data loss. Every scale ticket was captured the whole time -- it arrived late for about forty minutes, and every record has since been checked against each elevator's own log.

Why it happened: a security rule used an old label from before this service was renamed. It never matched correctly -- but caused no harm until real harvest traffic finally gave it something to break.
What's different now: the label lives in one place, a check blocks it from drifting apart again, and a background test watches the real connection every minute.
Up next: the dollar case for why that fix already paid for itself.
